events.title: August PPI (pipeline inflation print)
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline inflation 24 hours before CPI; with Brent above $100 and a hot August payrolls print, a hot PPI would harden the case for a September Fed hike.
events.what_to_watch: Core PPI m/m and the trade-services margin component, which feeds straight into core PCE.

events.title: ECB rate decision — 25bp hike to 2.50% deposit rate expected
events.why_it_matters: Markets price the hike as near-certain after eurozone headline CPI jumped to 3.3%; the reaction hinges on new staff projections and whether Lagarde signals a fourth move.
events.what_to_watch: 2027 inflation projection and any language closing the door on further hikes — swaps already price ~90bp of ECB tightening.

events.title: Oracle FQ1 2027 earnings (after close)
events.why_it_matters: The purest read on AI cloud-infrastructure demand and RPO backlog after a record Q4; consensus ~$19.1bn revenue and ~$1.30 EPS.
events.what_to_watch: OCI growth rate and the change in remaining performance obligations — the number that has driven the AI-infrastructure narrative.

events.title: Adobe FQ3 2026 earnings (after close)
events.why_it_matters: A bellwether for whether generative AI is cannibalizing creative-software seats; guidance is $6.67–6.72bn revenue with EPS ~$4.86–5.84 depending on GAAP basis.
events.what_to_watch: Digital Media ARR growth and any AI-monetization disclosure — the stock has been a serial post-earnings underperformer.

events.title: Macy's fiscal Q2 2026 earnings (pre-open)
events.why_it_matters: Depressed department-store read on the US consumer after July retail sales fell 0.6%; consensus ~$4.80bn revenue and ~$0.37 EPS.
events.what_to_watch: Comparable-store sales and gross margin — and any update on the previously disclosed accounting investigation.

events.title: August CPI (last major print before FOMC)
events.why_it_matters: The single most important input into the Sept 16 FOMC; consensus near 3.4% y/y headline with clear oil/war upside risk after a 162k payrolls beat.
events.what_to_watch: Core services ex-shelter and the energy pass-through — a hot core print would push hike odds well above the current ~55%.

events.title: FOMC decision, SEP/dot plot, Warsh press conference
events.why_it_matters: Markets price roughly a 54–60% chance of a 25bp hike — the first increase in years — after Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole keynote; the dot plot and reaction function matter more than the decision itself.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the SEP dots show a second hike in 2026 and how Warsh frames the oil shock: supply-side (look through) vs. expectations (act).

events.title: August advance retail sales
events.why_it_matters: July retail sales fell 0.6% m/m, the sharpest drop in over a year; a second weak print would sharpen the stagflation narrative feeding the FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Control-group sales, which strip autos/gas/building materials and feed directly into GDP nowcasts.

events.title: Bank of Japan decision (Sept 16–17) — hike to 1.25% priced
events.why_it_matters: A BOJ hike into a global risk-off, oil-shock backdrop is the classic yen-carry unwind trigger; Polymarket prices ~98% odds of a 25bp move to 1.25%.
events.what_to_watch: Ueda's guidance on the pace beyond September and any JGB purchase-taper language — a hawkish surprise would hit global duration and carry trades.

events.title: Bank of England decision (Sept 17) — hold at 3.75% expected
events.why_it_matters: BoE is expected to hold at 3.75% after a 6–3 vote in July, but the oil surge has revived hike bets and chief economist Huw Pill has publicly argued for 4%.
events.what_to_watch: The vote split — a shift toward more than three dissents would reprice GBP rates and sterling sharply.

events.title: September quadruple witching / quarterly options expiry
events.why_it_matters: Quarterly expiry of index futures, index options, stock options and single-stock futures lands two days after the FOMC, amplifying volume and pinning risk around a binary macro event.
events.what_to_watch: Dealer gamma positioning into the FOMC and any post-decision vol crush or squeeze.

events.title: FedEx FQ1 2027 earnings (Sept 17)
events.why_it_matters: The best single-company read on global goods demand and parcel pricing, arriving amid tariff-driven trade rerouting and a soft US consumer.
events.what_to_watch: FY guidance and any commentary on tariff-driven volume shifts and the FedEx Freight spin-off trajectory.

events.title: Trump–Xi Washington summit (Sept 24)
events.why_it_matters: Xi's state visit to the White House is the highest-stakes trade event of the quarter, covering tariffs, investment, AI, Taiwan and the Iran war — and lands less than six weeks before the US midterms.
events.what_to_watch: Whether China gets tariff relief in exchange for rare-earth licensing concessions, and whether any deal is framed as a 'win' ahead of the election.

events.title: UN General Assembly high-level week / General Debate
events.why_it_matters: UNGA 81 opens Sept 8 with General Debate from Sept 22; Xi is skipping it, but Iran, Ukraine, climate finance and trade will dominate headlines and side-deal risk.
events.what_to_watch: Any Iran ceasefire diplomacy on the margins and whether a Trump–Xi bilateral is confirmed for the same week.

events.title: US–Iran tanker war; Brent holds above $100, Hormuz traffic impaired
events.why_it_matters: Iran's largest missile/drone barrage since the April ceasefire, US strikes on Iranian crude carriers, and continued Hormuz disruption have pushed Brent above $100 and diesel to records — a direct stagflation input into the FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Whether tanker traffic resumes through Hormuz or the conflict widens to Gulf producers; any ceasefire mediation via Pakistan or Oman.

events.title: US Section 338 tariffs on Canada escalate to outright import bans Sept 29
events.why_it_matters: The US moves from 50% Section 338 duties to outright bans on certain Canadian dairy, alcohol and motor-vehicle imports effective Sept 29, with no USMCA exemption — Canada has already matched dollar-for-dollar on $27.6bn of goods.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the bans are delayed in negotiation and how far the retaliation list extends into autos and energy.

events.title: Canada's retaliatory counter-tariffs in force
events.why_it_matters: Canada imposed 15%, 25% and 50% tariffs on US goods effective Sept 8, matching US Section 338/232 rates product-by-product — a live, escalating two-way trade shock inside the USMCA bloc.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the USMCA joint review process becomes the off-ramp or the next escalation venue.

events.title: USMCA 2026 joint review process ongoing
events.why_it_matters: The mandated six-year review governs $1.8tn in trilateral trade; with Section 338 bans live, the review is now the main venue where North American supply-chain rules could be rewritten or torn up.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the US tables automotive rules-of-origin changes and whether Mexico's posture shifts after the Canadian escalation.

events.title: OPEC+ holds October output policy unchanged
events.why_it_matters: The seven core members kept September quota levels for October, declining to add barrels into a $100 Brent market while they negotiate new baseline quotas — spare capacity is the only thing capping the oil spike.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the group accelerates unwinding or, conversely, signals it will defend $100; next meeting cadence and new quota baselines.

events.title: August employment report: +162k, unemployment 4.1%
events.why_it_matters: Payrolls crushed the ~53k consensus and the 12-month average of 31k, lifting September hike odds to ~60% and pushing 10-year yields toward 4.8% — the print that turned the FOMC into a live meeting.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the strength persists into the September report and whether wage growth re-accelerates alongside the oil shock.

top_risks: Hot August CPI on Sept 11 pushing September Fed hike odds materially above 55% and triggering a broad risk-off repricing
US–Iran tanker war escalating further, with Brent above $100 and Hormuz disruption feeding a global stagflation shock
BOJ hike into a risk-off, oil-shock backdrop triggering a yen-carry unwind and global duration selloff
US Section 338 import bans on Canada effective Sept 29 escalating into a broader North American trade war inside USMCA
Trump–Xi summit on Sept 24 failing to produce tariff relief, reviving trade-war escalation ahead of the US midterms
top_opportunities: Energy and defense exposure if Hormuz disruption persists and Brent holds above $100
AI cloud-infrastructure names if Oracle's OCI growth and RPO backlog beat expectations
Rate-sensitive financials if the FOMC delivers a hawkish hike with a steeper dot plot
Volatility and options strategies around Sept 18 quadruple witching and the FOMC
North American trade-deal beneficiaries if the USMCA review produces an off-ramp to the Section 338 escalation
summary: The scan is dominated by a live September FOMC (Sept 16) with hike odds near 55–60% after a blowout August payrolls print, a hot PPI today and CPI tomorrow, and an oil shock from the US–Iran tanker war keeping Brent above $100. Central bank decisions from the ECB (today), BOJ (Sept 16–17) and BoE (Sept 17) cluster around the Fed, while a heavy earnings slate (Oracle, Adobe, Macy's, FedEx) and the Sept 24 Trump–Xi summit add idiosyncratic and geopolitical risk. North American trade tensions are escalating with Canada's counter-tariffs in force and US Section 338 import bans due Sept 29, and Sept 18 quadruple witching amplifies positioning risk around the FOMC.
